title: Exam Technique and Final Review

header.html: exam strategy and review of every domain
the commands in this module were used in the executed labs of Modules 0 to 13 (Kubernetes v1.37.0)

toc.title: Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)

html:
1The time budget

The exam is 2 hours for 15 to 20 tasks. That is an average of 6 to 8 minutes per task, with the passing score at 66%. Points differ per task (the exact points per task are not published on the pages used for this course), so:

Rule Why
Spend the first 2 minutes skimming the whole list if the interface allows; otherwise start in order find the quick wins early
Do easy tasks first, flag hard ones one 15-minute task can cost two easy ones
If you are stuck after about 6 minutes, flag it and move on partial progress on many tasks beats perfection on few
Keep 10 minutes at the end to re-verify a typo in a namespace costs a full task
Do not leave a task half-broken (a half-edited manifest) the checker sees the final state

Where the points are (by domain weight): Troubleshooting 30%, Architecture 25%, Networking 20%, Workloads 15%, Storage 10%. Storage tasks are few and usually quick; Troubleshooting tasks are many and vary in length.

2The routine for every task

  1. Read the whole task, including the last line (names, namespaces, "do not change ...").
  2. Run the context line (kubectl config use-context ...). Check with k config current-context.
  3. Note exact names, namespaces, ports, labels, file paths. Copy them from the task text, never retype from memory.
  4. Do it with the fastest tool (imperative command, --dry-run=client -o yaml, kubectl explain, one docs page).
  5. Verify with a different command from the one that created it (create with k create, verify with k get -o wide/describe/a test Pod).
  6. Move on.

3Using the documentation well

You may use kubernetes.io/docs and blog, helm.sh/docs and gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io (CKA only), the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under /usr/share. You may use the kubernetes.io search; you must not open results from outside the allowed sites.

  • Learn where things are before the exam: Concepts for explanations, Tasks for step-by-step YAML (RBAC, PV/PVC, probes, NetworkPolicy, etcd backup under "Administer a Cluster", Ingress, Gateway API), Reference for kubectl cheat sheet and kubeadm commands.
  • Prefer kubectl explain for field names (faster than the browser).
  • Copy examples, then change names; do not retype a long YAML.
  • Browser tabs and the terminal share the screen; practice with only the allowed pages.

4Domain checklists

Troubleshooting (30%): get, describe, logs --previous, get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp; nodes: systemctl, journalctl -u kubelet; control plane: crictl ps -a, crictl logs, manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests; services: selector, endpoints, targetPort, DNS, NetworkPolicy; kubectl top.

Cluster Architecture (25%): RBAC (create role/rolebinding ... --verb --resource, auth can-i), kubeadm (token create --print-join-command, certs check-expiration, upgrade order), etcd (snapshot save with endpoint and three cert flags, etcdutl snapshot restore, edit the data-dir path in the manifest, restart control plane components), Helm (install/upgrade/rollback/template), Kustomize (apply -k), CRDs, drain/cordon.

Services and Networking (20%): Services (expose, types, ports), DNS names, Ingress (class, host/path, pathType), Gateway API (GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute), NetworkPolicy (AND versus OR, DNS for egress), CoreDNS.

Workloads and Scheduling (15%): rollouts (set image, rollout undo), ConfigMap/Secret, probes, resources, LimitRange/ResourceQuota, labels/selectors/affinity/taints, DaemonSet/StatefulSet/Job, HPA.

Storage (10%): PV/PVC binding rules, StorageClass default and reclaim policy, access modes, WaitForFirstConsumer.

5Common traps (each one cost a point in a lab)

Trap Defence
Wrong cluster context run and verify the context line
Wrong namespace (object created in default) -n on every command, or set the context namespace; verify with get -A | grep name
Resource created but misspelled name copy names from the task
Pod fields immutable delete and recreate (--force --grace-period 0)
ClusterRole + RoleBinding scope RoleBinding = one namespace
roleRef immutable delete and recreate the binding
NetworkPolicy blocks DNS allow UDP/TCP 53 in egress
Selector typo = no endpoints get endpointslices, --show-labels
Edited a static Pod manifest wrongly back up first, then crictl logs
etcd restore without pointing the Pod at the new directory edit the hostPath in the etcd manifest
Forgot to restart control plane components after an etcd restore restart apiserver, controller manager, scheduler
Used a toleration and expected placement combine with nodeSelector/affinity
Left a typo-free but unverified answer verify every task
Rebooted base or used the Insert key not allowed

6The final week

  • Redo the break-and-fix labs (Troubleshooting is 30%) until you can do each in under 6 minutes.
  • Run the two timed mixed sets (Modules 14 and 15) under exam conditions: 2 hours, only the allowed documentation.
  • Use the killer.sh simulator that comes with the exam registration (2 attempts of 36 hours each): it is the closest to the real environment, including the ssh <node> workflow this course imitates with docker exec.
  • Practice the speed kit (Module 0) until k, $do and kubectl explain are automatic.
  • Re-read the Quick Reference Cards of every module.
  • Check the current curriculum version and exam page before booking: the exam moves to a new Kubernetes version every few months; rules, fees and allowed resources can change.

7Recall questions

R1How much time per task do you have on average?

Show the answer

About 6 to 8 minutes (2 hours for 15 to 20 tasks).

R2What should you do after about 6 minutes on a stuck task?

Show the answer

Flag it and move on; return at the end.

R3What is the first thing you do in each task?

Show the answer

Run the context line and note exact names and namespaces.

R4Name two fast ways to avoid hand-writing YAML.

Show the answer

--dry-run=client -o yaml and copying examples from the documentation.

R5Which tool beats the browser for field names?

Show the answer

kubectl explain.

R6What is the passing score?

Show the answer

66%.

R7After an etcd restore, what must you do besides pointing the etcd Pod at the new data directory?

Show the answer

Restart the API server, controller manager and scheduler so they drop stale caches.

R8Which simulator is included with the exam registration?

Show the answer

killer.sh (2 attempts of 36 hours each).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Time 2 hours, 15-20 tasks, about 6-8 minutes each, 66% to pass
Order easy first, flag hard, 10 minutes to verify
Every task context line, exact names, verify with a second command
Docs kubernetes.io, helm.sh, gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io only
Weights T 30, A 25, N 20, W 15, S 10
Practice break-and-fix labs, timed sets, killer.sh
